Quick Read

Corning (GLW) has beaten EPS estimates five straight quarters, yet shares have fallen 12%, 9%, and 5% on each of the last three earnings days.

JPMorgan analysts said strong Q3 revenue could put Corning on track to hit its $20 billion run-rate target ahead of schedule.

Corning's Optical Communications segment, fueled by deals with Meta and NVIDIA, must sustain 30%-plus growth to justify a valuation of roughly 38x 2026 earnings.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

Corning (NYSE:GLW) reports third-quarter results before the open on Tuesday, Oct. 27. The stock is down 19.93% over the past month. This report needs to show that AI fiber demand still supports a premium valuation.

Shutterstock
Earnings Beats Keep Coming While Shares Keep Flinching

Last quarter, core EPS of $0.78 beat the $0.7538 estimate. That was Corning's fifth consecutive EPS beat. Revenue of $4.505 billion missed the $4.63 billion consensus even after growing 16.6%. Shares fell 12.1% on earnings day, then gained 26.89% over the following week.

GLW Earnings Explorer — 24/7 Wall St.

Optical Communications led the quarter with $2.072 billion in sales, up 32%. Enterprise Networks grew 65% on Gen AI demand. Core operating margin expanded 190 bps to 20.9%, and management upgraded its Springboard Plan to target annualized sales run rates of $20 billion by the end of 2026, $30 billion by 2028, and $40 billion by 2030.

Since then, the stock has slid 1.66% to $123.62. The shares still trade at about 38x 2026 consensus EPS.

title: Newmont And 2 Other Great Undervalued Stocks

Newmont And 2 Other Great Undervalued Stocks

Evercore recently highlighted specific credit and Treasury yield levels that could trigger a shakeout in highly priced AI stocks, which leaves a lot of investors exposed to companies that rely heavily on borrowed money. Cash rich businesses that trade below what their future cash flows suggest they are worth suddenly look more interesting. This article breaks down three such ideas from our cash flow valuation screener and explains why they may deserve a closer look.

The three undervalued cash flow stocks covered below are just a sample, since the full screen surfaced 458 more companies with equally compelling stories that are not covered in this article.

If you want to identify and analyze those additional ideas with the same lens used here, head straight into the Undervalued Stocks Based On Cash Flows screener to filter for the opportunities that best match your convictions.

Newmont (NEM)

Newmont is a global gold producer whose bullion output underpins the cash flows used in DCF work for this screener, with additional exposure to copper and other metals and a market value of about US$118.9b.

Gold investors watching cash flows closely will care about how Newmont is trying to keep its operations efficient, protect profitability and squeeze more out of its asset base over time.

"Newmont's focus on operational stability, cost discipline, and productivity enhancements (for example, at Lihir, Boddington, and across its core assets) is expected to drive lower operating costs and improved EBITDA margins, positioning the company for margin expansion and stronger net income over time."

What really matters next is how a single moving piece in this setup ultimately shapes the durability of those cash rich margins.

That resilience question sits at the center of the full narrative for Newmont, which maps how Newmont's cash engine could react if gold prices or costs start to decouple.

NEM Discounted Cash Flow as at Oct 2026
Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A)

Berkshire Hathaway is a sprawling Omaha based conglomerate whose insurance units anchor the cash flow story for this screener, while large contributions also come from manufacturing at about US$83.0b, BNSF rail at US$24.6b, retailing and services at US$44.7b, and a market value near US$1.2t.

For investors focused on cash flow driven value, Berkshire Hathaway offers something unusual in this list: a mix of insurance float, rail, utilities, and manufacturing that all feed into a single capital allocation machine.

"The company's cash and short-term Treasuries hit a staggering, record-breaking $397.4 billion."
